title: Mathematics on arXiv — rolling 30-day report
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This is an inferred notable-paper selection, not a readership ranking; citation evidence for these recent papers is sparse.

sections.title: The maximum relaxation time of a random walk on regular graphs
sections.abstract: The paper gives sharp quadratic extremal bounds for random-walk relaxation time on connected regular graphs and reports resolutions of several associated graph-spectral conjectures.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims leading relaxation-time constants 3/(2π²) for even and 1/π² for odd graph orders, identifies extremizing regular-graph chains for sufficiently large order, and reports sharp algebraic-connectivity, stability, hitting-time, and commute-time results.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite, simple, undirected connected graphs. Relaxation-time extremal statements concern regular graphs; other theorems impose their stated minimum-degree or fixed-degree conditions.
sections.unique_caveat: The unique-extremizer statement is for sufficiently large order; subsidiary sharp bounds have separate hypotheses.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract names the Aldous–Fill spectral-gap conjecture and several structural/uniqueness conjectures; the current version is described as substantially expanded.

sections.title: A Complete Resolution of Forsythe's Conjecture for Restarted Conjugate Gradients
sections.abstract: For exact restarted conjugate gradients on real symmetric positive-definite systems, the authors classify which restart lengths force even/odd residual-direction convergence and construct counterexamples above the threshold.
sections.claimed_result: In exact arithmetic, restart lengths 2 and 3 either terminate or have convergent even and odd normalized residual directions; for every s≥4, a nonterminating diagonal positive-definite counterexample exists in dimension s+4. The universal claim holds exactly for s∈{1,2,3}.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite-dimensional real symmetric positive-definite matrices, arbitrary initial data, and exact arithmetic; counterexamples are diagonal.
sections.unique_caveat: This is an asymptotic direction result, not a finite-precision guarantee or a practical solver convergence-rate estimate.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper gives a sharp classification, spans three mathematical categories, and reports a Lean formalization.

sections.title: A counterexample to the quantum Hedetniemi conjecture
sections.abstract: Explicit finite graphs violate the conjectured equality between the quantum chromatic number of a categorical product and the smaller quantum chromatic number of its factors.
sections.claimed_result: The authors construct G,H with χ(G×H)≤1538 while min(χq(G),χq(H))≥1539, disproving the conjecture and extending failure to spatial, approximate, commuting-operator, and C*-algebraic variants.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite simple graphs and the quantum-coloring models defined in the paper; the headline construction is explicit but very large.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is a counterexample to a specific product identity, not a general formula for quantum chromatic numbers; the headline construction uses graphs with over a million vertices.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper gives an explicit numerical gap, is cross-listed in combinatorics and quantum physics, and reports Lean 4 formalization.

sections.title: Sharp Hessian integrability for fully nonlinear elliptic supersolutions in low dimensions
sections.abstract: The authors settle the planar sharp Hessian-integrability conjecture and obtain the matching three-dimensional exponent for ellipticity ratios from 1 through 4.
sections.claimed_result: For viscosity supersolutions of fully nonlinear uniformly elliptic equations, the authors claim ε₂(κ)=2/(κ+1) in dimension two and ε₃(κ)=3/(2κ+1) in dimension three for 1≤κ≤4, where κ=Λ/λ.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The W²,ε regularity theory for viscosity supersolutions of fully nonlinear uniformly elliptic equations, with ellipticity ratio κ=Λ/λ.
sections.unique_caveat: In dimension three, the abstract reports a lower bound and a remaining gap beyond κ=4; it does not claim the optimal exponent is settled there.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract gives an explicit optimal exponent and the exact parameter range reached in dimension three.

sections.title: Sign patterns of real powers of infinite products: resolution of four conjectures of Schlosser and Zhou
sections.abstract: The paper resolves four conjectures on coefficient-sign patterns for specified powers of four q-products, including precise parameter intervals where several conjectures fail.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims one conjecture is true and three fail on explicitly specified intervals, using exact cusp analysis, explicit Hardy–Ramanujan–Rademacher expansions, and certified exact/ball-arithmetic checks.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Coefficient signs of powers of four specified Goellnitz–Gordon/Borwein infinite products, in the parameter ranges stated in the paper.
sections.unique_caveat: The conclusions cover these four products and conjectures, not sign patterns for arbitrary infinite products; some finite-range claims depend on certified computation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It settles four named conjectures, pinpoints exact failure intervals and thresholds, and reports code plus certificates for computational components.

sections.title: Nonmaximal sums of maximally monotone operators under Rockafellar's constraint qualification
sections.abstract: The author constructs maximally monotone operator pairs satisfying an interior-domain condition whose sum is not maximally monotone, and develops constructions that transfer counterexamples across Banach spaces.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims a complete disproof of Rockafellar's sum conjecture under the stated interior-domain condition, with a general construction theorem and counterexample families on Banach spaces containing or admitting suitable c₀/ℓ¹ subspaces or quotients.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Pairs of maximally monotone operators on Banach spaces satisfying the paper's interior-domain condition; transfer results have additional subspace/quotient hypotheses.
sections.unique_caveat: This refutes the stated condition's sufficiency; it does not imply that every stronger sum theorem or constraint qualification fails.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The latest version is substantially reorganized around a general construction and pullback theorem, directly addressing a named conjecture; it is cross-listed in functional analysis and machine learning.

sections.title: Sharp connectivity thresholds for mixed rigidity packings and improved bounds for highly connected orientations of graphs
sections.abstract: A unified connectivity theorem packs edge-disjoint rigid spanning subgraphs at a sharp threshold in the stated range and improves quadratic upper bounds for highly connected graph orientations.
sections.claimed_result: Every graph with connectivity at least Σᵢdᵢ(dᵢ+1) contains pairwise edge-disjoint spanning dᵢ-rigid subgraphs; the bound is sharp when the sum is at least 4. The paper also gives the stated improved orientation bounds.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Positive integers d₁,…,dₛ and finite graphs satisfying the specified vertex-connectivity threshold; sharpness is claimed when Σᵢdᵢ(dᵢ+1)≥4.
sections.unique_caveat: Sharpness is not asserted in the abstract for the smaller-sum cases; the orientation statements are upper bounds, not a complete determination of the optimal function.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors claim to settle two sharp packing conjectures, prove a general mixed-dimension theorem, and reduce the leading coefficient in a related orientation bound from 320 to 25/2 (and to 8 asymptotically).

sections.title: A weak Hellinger inequality for noisy Boolean channels
sections.abstract: For the binary symmetric channel, the authors prove a weak Hellinger-conjecture form in which dictators maximize Hellinger Φ-entropy among Boolean inputs and one-bit noisy-output statistics.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove the stated weak form using an explicit three-parameter inequality, polynomial approximations, and computer-assisted positivity checks; they report Lean 4 formal verification.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The result is for the binary symmetric channel, Boolean input functions, and one-bit statistics of the noisy output.
sections.unique_caveat: This is explicitly a weak form for a restricted channel/statistic setting; it should not be described as settling the full Hellinger conjecture.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper is cross-listed in information theory and combinatorics, has a substantive v2 revision, and reports computer-assisted checks plus Lean formalization.

sections.title: Maker Breaker Games on a Budget
sections.abstract: In a budget-enabled version of the Maker–Breaker triangle game, the authors determine the exact threshold bias and give an asymptotic threshold when accumulated budget cannot be spent on threats.
sections.claimed_result: In the budget version, the triangle-game threshold is exactly ⌈√(2n−2)−3/2⌉; without spending budget on threats it is (√2+o(1))√n. The paper also gives first explicit bounds for the K₄ game.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Maker claims one edge per round in Kₙ and Breaker's bias is q; the exact formula applies to the newly defined budget game, with a distinct result for the threat-restricted rule.
sections.unique_caveat: The exact threshold is for the budget variant; the original triangle-game threshold remains open in the abstract's stated context.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract identifies an exact threshold matching the known lower bound in the new budget variant and adds a threat-restricted asymptotic result.
